issue.title: Published blog posts still tell readers to run bare 'uv tool install sase', which resolves to sase 0.1.0
issue.description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-1le.3 (applicability, PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note #1); triaged by the sase-1le land agent on 2026-10-16.

The documented install command is single-sourced as `uv tool install "sase>=0.18"` (tools/render_applicability, decision install_command = floor), but the two published blog posts still carry bare commands:

- `docs/blog/posts/structured-agentic-software-engineering.md` lines 328, 339, 409 (`uv tool install sase`, `uv tool install sase --with sase-github`). This launch essay is linked from the homepage footer and is part of the curated handbook PDF.
- `docs/blog/posts/why-coding-agents-need-orchestration.md` lines 93, 101, 109, 116 (bare plus `--with sase-github` / `--with sase-telegram` variants).

Today the bare command does not install a current SASE: `echo sase | uv pip compile - --python-version 3.12` resolves `sase==0.1.0` (PyPI latest is 0.17.1, which is uninstallable per sase-16p), while the floored form fails loudly with a resolver error until 0.18 ships.

Fix direction: change each bare command in those two posts to the floored form (keeping the `--with` plugin flags), or replace the fences with a link to /start/install/. Decide whether dated essays should be listed in tools/render_applicability DOCUMENTED_COMMAND_FILES so a future floor bump updates them too. Do not touch Guide pages; they already carry the generated command.

task_type_fields.impact: A reader who copies the launch essay's or the orchestration post's install command gets the 2025 0.1.0 package instead of a loud resolver error, which defeats the install_command = floor decision.
task_type_fields.repro: grep -n 'uv tool install sase' docs/blog/posts/*.md; then echo sase | uv pip compile - --python-version 3.12 resolves sase==0.1.0

issue.creation_reason: Phase sase-1le.3 proposed it and the sase-1le lander confirmed it: the launch essay is linked from the homepage and included in the handbook PDF, yet its install command bypasses the documented version floor.
